name: Captain Advance Filter
author: Devang Vachheta

sections.description:
Captain Advance Filter is a lightweight WordPress search and filter plugin that lets you create powerful AJAX powered filters for posts, pages, custom post types, and WooCommerce products.

Create advanced search and filtering experiences without coding. Build custom queries and filter sets, choose from multiple filter types and display styles, and show filtered results instantly without reloading the page.

Filter your content by categories, tags, custom taxonomies, post meta, product attributes, price, stock status, ratings, dates, and more. Display filter options using checkboxes, radio buttons, dropdowns, search fields, range sliders, A Z navigation, date pickers, WooCommerce ratings, or a frontend view switcher.

Use the visual Query Builder and Filter Set Builder to create reusable filtering systems, then display them anywhere using shortcodes, Gutenberg blocks, or Elementor widgets.

Watch the Plugin Overview Video | YouTube Tutorials | Facebook Community | X | Free Support

✨ Core Features:

  • AJAX Search & Filtering: Update results instantly without a page reload.
  • Visual Query Builder: Create custom queries for posts, pages, custom post types, and products.
  • Filter Set Builder: Combine multiple filters and connect them to a reusable query.
  • Multiple Filter Types: Checkbox, Radio, Pill Tabs, Dropdown, Search, Range, A Z, Date Picker, Woo Rating, and View Switcher.
  • Taxonomy & Meta Filtering: Filter content using categories, tags, custom taxonomies, custom fields, and post meta.
  • WooCommerce Product Filters: Filter products by attributes, price, stock status, and star ratings.
  • Multiple Display Styles: List, Buttons, Color Swatches, Image Swatches, Tabs, and Pill Tabs for supported filters.
  • AJAX Pagination: Choose from numbered Pagination, Load More, Infinite Scroll, or None.
  • SEO-Friendly Server-Side Rendering: The first page of results, pagination links, result counts, and filters are part of the page HTML, so search engines can read every result and visitors see content without waiting. Every results page has its own crawlable URL.
  • AJAX Loader Styles: Choose Spinner, Overlay, Skeleton, or None for AJAX result loading.
  • Frontend View Switcher: Let visitors switch between available grid column layouts.
  • Category & Search Archives: Place a grid in a category, tag, or WooCommerce product category template, or on the search results page, and it automatically shows only that archive’s posts.
  • Shareable Filter URLs: Share and bookmark filtered results with selected filter values preserved in the URL.
  • Result Count: Display the number of matching results with a dedicated shortcode.
  • Custom Result Cards: Choose from predefined card styles, including the new Boutique product card, or create custom card templates.
  • Wishlist: Let visitors save items with a heart icon and view them on a Wishlist page using a shortcode or Elementor widget.
  • Responsive Grid Layouts: Control desktop, tablet, and mobile columns.
  • Slider Layout: Show your cards as a slider with three styles: Equal Cards, Spotlight, and Carousel.
  • Style Controls: Design your cards from the Style tab with color pickers, responsive typography, borders, shadows, spacing, and slider arrow, dot, and progress styling.
  • Elementor Support: Dedicated Filter, Grid, Pagination, and Wishlist widgets.
  • Gutenberg Support: Native blocks for Filter, Grid, and Pagination.
  • Shortcode Support: Easily embed filters, grids, pagination, result counts, and the wishlist anywhere.
  • Query Caching: Optional caching using WordPress transients for faster repeated queries, set per query with its own cache duration and a one-click Clear Cache button.
  • Dark Mode: Clean and modern React powered admin dashboard with Dark Mode support.
  • No Coding Required: Build queries and filters directly from the WordPress admin dashboard.

🔎 Filter Types:

  • Checkbox: Select one or multiple options.
  • Radio: Select a single option.
  • Pill Tabs: A row of rounded tabs with an “All” tab first, ideal for a category switcher above your results.
  • Dropdown: Choose filter values from a dropdown.
  • Search: Search and filter content using keywords.
  • Range: Create numeric range filters such as price ranges, as Min / Max number fields or a two-handle slider.
  • A Z: Browse content alphabetically.
  • Date Picker: Filter content by publish date ranges.
  • Woo Rating: Filter WooCommerce products by star rating.
  • View Switcher: Allow visitors to switch between available result grid layouts.

🎨 Display Styles:

Checkbox and Radio filters can use multiple display styles depending on the selected data source:

  • List
  • Buttons
  • Color Swatches
  • Image Swatches
  • Tabs
  • Pill Tabs

Color and Image Swatches can automatically use WooCommerce attribute swatch data when available, with fallback options when swatch data is not configured.

📄 Pagination & Loading:

Choose how filtered results are displayed and loaded:

  • Pagination: Standard numbered pagination.
  • Load More: Load additional results without leaving the page.
  • Infinite Scroll: Automatically load more results while scrolling.
  • None: Display results without pagination controls.

Choose an AJAX loading indicator for each query:

  • Spinner
  • Overlay
  • Skeleton
  • None

🛒 WooCommerce Compatibility:

Captain Advance Filter works with WooCommerce and provides dedicated product filtering features.

  • Woo Rating: Filter products by N stars & up using WooCommerce product ratings.
  • Price Range: Filter products using WooCommerce price data.
  • Stock Status: Filter products by available stock status.
  • Product Attributes: Filter by attributes such as color, brand, size, and more.
  • Color Swatches: Display product attribute options as color swatches.
  • Image Swatches: Display product attribute options using images.
  • Shop Card: Display WooCommerce product price, sale badge, and Add to Cart button.
  • Boutique Card: A product card with a category label, badges, wishlist heart, price, description, and an Add to Bag button whose label you can change. Captain Advance Filter Pro adds a second, more refined style called Elegant Boutique.
  • Custom Product Templates: Use WooCommerce specific tokens such as {{price}}, {{sale_badge}}, and {{add_to_cart}}.

🧩 Custom Post Type Support:

Use Captain Advance Filter with any publicly viewable WordPress post type. Create custom queries and filter results using taxonomies, post meta, dates, search terms, and other supported filter sources.

🔌 Builder Integrations:

  • Elementor: Dedicated Filter, Grid, Pagination, and Wishlist widgets with Elementor styling controls.
  • Gutenberg: Native blocks for Filter, Grid, and Pagination.
  • Shortcodes: Use Captain Advance Filter with any WordPress page builder or theme that supports shortcodes.
  • Bricks Builder: Support coming soon.

⚡ Performance:

  • Lightweight frontend implementation.
  • AJAX powered filtering without full page reloads.
  • Frontend assets are loaded only on pages where Captain Advance Filter is used.
  • No jQuery dependency on the frontend.
  • Optional query result caching using WordPress transients.
  • Native lazy loading support for result card images.

🔗 Shortcodes:

  • [captaf-filter id="1"] : Display a filter set.
  • [captaf-grid query="query_key"] : Display the filtered content grid.
  • [captaf-pagination query="query_key"] : Display pagination controls.
  • [captaf-count query="query_key"] : Display the matching result count.
  • [captaf-wishlist] : Display the visitor’s saved wishlist items.
  • [captaf-clear-filters query="query_key"] : A standalone “Clear Filters” button you can place anywhere on the page – top, bottom, wherever – instead of relying on the automatic active-filters bar above the filter widget. Optional text="Reset" for custom button text, hide_empty="no" to keep it always visible instead of only appearing once a filter is active.

You can also display individual filters from a Filter Set using the only attribute.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin from the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Open Captain Advance Filter from the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Create a Query using the Query Builder.
  5. Create a Filter Set and connect it to your Query.
  6. Configure your filter types, display styles, pagination, and loader settings.
  7. Add the generated shortcode to your page or use the Elementor or Gutenberg integration.
sections.faq:
Does Captain Advance Filter work without Elementor?

Yes. Elementor is optional. You can use Captain Advance Filter with Gutenberg blocks, shortcodes, or any WordPress theme that supports shortcodes.

How does the Wishlist work?

Turn it on from the Wishlist page in the plugin menu, then add the [captaf-wishlist] shortcode (or the “Captain Wishlist” Elementor widget) to any page. Visitors save items with a heart icon on your cards. By default saved items live in the visitor’s own browser, so nothing is stored on your server. Captain Advance Filter Pro can also save them to the visitor’s account, and items saved as a guest are moved into their account when they log in.

Can I show the Range filter as a slider?

Yes. In Filter Sets, choose the Range filter type, then set Range Style to Slider. You can set the step and add a prefix or suffix such as $ or km.

Can I hide or move the “N filters active” bar?

Yes. The bar is a filter type called “Active Filters Bar”. In Filter Sets, drag it to where it should show, or delete it to hide the bar.

Is it SEO friendly?

Yes. With Server-Side Rendering (Settings > SEO & Page Speed, on by default) the first page of results is part of the page HTML, with real titles, images, and links that search engines can read without running JavaScript. Pagination uses real links, so every results page can be crawled and has its own canonical URL. Filtering and pagination still update instantly with AJAX for visitors.

Can the grid show only the current category’s products?

Yes. In the query, turn on “Match Current Archive Page” (Step 1). When the grid is placed in a category, tag, or other taxonomy archive template (for example a WooCommerce product category template), or on the search results page, it shows only that archive’s posts.

My security plugin blocks the WordPress REST API. Will filtering still work?

Yes. If the REST API is blocked for visitors, filtering, pagination, and the wishlist automatically switch to WordPress’s admin-ajax instead, with the same checks.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. Captain Advance Filter supports WooCommerce product filtering by attributes, price, stock status, and product ratings. WooCommerce specific Shop Card and swatch options are also available.

Can I filter custom post types?

Yes. Any publicly viewable WordPress post type can be used as a Query source.

Can I filter by custom fields or post meta?

Yes. Filters can use supported post meta fields as a data source in addition to taxonomies.

Does it support AJAX filtering?

Yes. Filtered results are loaded using AJAX without requiring a full page reload.

What pagination options are available?

You can choose between numbered Pagination, Load More, Infinite Scroll, or None.

What loader styles are available?

You can choose Spinner, Overlay, Skeleton, or None for AJAX result loading.

How do I show my results as a slider?

In the Query editor, go to Select Layout, click Slider next to Grid, and choose a style: Equal Cards, Spotlight (bigger middle card), or Carousel (counter and progress bar). The slides are your Posts Per Page, and the Columns and Gap settings decide how many cards show at once. Pagination is not used with the slider.

Can visitors switch between grid layouts?

Yes. Add the View Switcher filter type to allow visitors to switch between the available frontend grid column layouts.

Can I create shareable filtered URLs?

Yes. Enable the Shareable URL option for supported filters to sync selected filter values with the page URL. Visitors can share or bookmark filtered results.

Do I need coding knowledge?

No. Queries and Filter Sets can be created using the visual admin dashboard. Shortcodes are generated automatically.

Will Captain Advance Filter slow down my website?

The plugin uses conditional asset loading so frontend assets are only loaded on pages where Captain Advance Filter is actually used. Optional query caching is also available to improve repeated searches.

Are the frontend REST endpoints secure?

Yes. The filtering endpoints verify that queried post types and taxonomies are publicly viewable before returning results. Private data is not exposed through these endpoints.
sections.changelog:
1.6.4

  • New : Collapsible Sidebar : The admin menu can now be collapsed to icons only with the arrow button next to the logo. When collapsed, hover the logo to get the expand button. Your choice is remembered.
  • New : Plugin Overview Video : A quick walkthrough video is now shown on the Dashboard, the Documentation page (overview and Quick Start), and the Help page. Clicking it opens the video on YouTube in a new tab.
  • Improved : Filter Set Editor in 2 Steps : The Filter Set editor now has two steps, Filters and Insert Code. The last step shows the filter set shortcode and a PHP snippet for your child theme, with the shortcodes of each single filter in a list below. The shortcode box inside each filter was removed.
  • Improved : Filter Set Auto-Save : Filter sets are saved automatically while you edit, so the Update button was removed.
  • Improved : Filter Set Editor Remembers Its Place : The editor keeps the filter set and the step in the page URL, so a reload or a shared link opens the same filter set on the same step.
  • Improved : Settings and Wishlist Auto-Save : The Settings page and the Wishlist page now save as soon as you change a switch or the Storage Mode, so their Save Settings buttons were removed.
  • Improved : Boutique Is the Default Card Style : New queries start with the Boutique card style when WooCommerce is active (Classic otherwise).
  • Improved : Default Card Gap : New queries start with a 15px gap between cards.
  • Improved : Random Default Query Key : New queries get a default key with a short random ending (for example query_k3x9a), so it can never clash with an existing query. You can still edit the key.
  • Improved : Slider Preview in Select Layout : With Slider turned on, every Card Style preview in the query editor shows the selected slider style with its arrows and dots (or counter and progress bar for Style 3).
  • Fix : Slider Style 2 (Spotlight) : Every click on the arrows now slides the posts by one place. Before, the first click only moved the highlight to the second post while the posts stayed still. The first and last posts now show as neighbours of the highlighted post, and the arrows stay just outside the big middle card, on its left and right.
  • Fix : Slider Style 2 Preview : The Style 2 preview in the query editor now looks like the real slider: bigger middle card, dimmed side cards, arrows next to the middle card. The Style 1 preview arrows now sit on the card edges as well.
  • Fix : Queries List Not Updating : A query you just created could be missing from the Queries list (and its key then showed “already in use”) when you left the editor through the sidebar instead of Finish. The list now refreshes after every save and whenever the editor closes.
  • Fix : Editor Spacing : The Filter Set editor now has the same page padding as the query editor, and the Performance card in the query Settings step has even spacing between its rows.
  • Fix : Long Plugin Name in Menu : A long plugin name in the admin menu now wraps onto a second line instead of being cut off.

1.6.3

  • New : Active Filters Bar Filter Type : The “N filters active – Clear all” bar is now a filter type you place anywhere in a Filter Set (above, between, or below your filters), or leave out. Existing filter sets keep their bar: it appears as the first filter when you edit them.
  • Improved : Simpler Filter Set Editor : Cancel and Update buttons moved to the top of the page and saving keeps you in the editor, the separate Clear Filters shortcode box was removed (use the Clear Filters Button filter type), the technical Key field is hidden (keys are created from the label), filter types that don’t use a data source (A-Z, Search, Date Picker, Woo Rating, View Switcher, Clear Filters, Active Filters Bar) no longer show the Source Type and Data Source fields, and the Filter Sets list shows only the filter shortcode (the grid shortcode is on the Queries page).
  • New : Match Current Archive Page : A new query option (Step 1) makes the grid show only the posts of the category, tag, or taxonomy archive it is placed on (for example a WooCommerce product category template), or the results of the current search.
  • New : REST API Fallback : When a security plugin blocks the WordPress REST API for visitors, filtering, pagination, and the wishlist automatically switch to admin-ajax, so they keep working.
  • New : Readable Filter Keys : New filters get a key based on their label (for example “Product Brand” becomes product_brand) instead of a number, so shareable filter URLs are easy to read. Keys of existing filters are not changed.
  • Improved : Smaller Frontend Files : The frontend scripts and styles now load as minified files, about 55% smaller for the main script. The original files are still used when SCRIPT_DEBUG is on.
  • Fix : Custom Template Saving : Saving a query removed every HTML tag from its Custom Template, leaving only the placeholders. Templates now keep their HTML (unsafe code such as scripts is still removed). Templates saved with an earlier version need to be entered again.
  • New : Server-Side Rendering : The first page of results, its pagination, the result count, and the filter options are now part of the page HTML, so search engines can read every result and visitors see content right away instead of a loading spinner. Filtering and pagination still update instantly with AJAX. Can be turned off under Settings > SEO & Page Speed.
  • New : Crawlable Pagination : Pagination and Load More now use real links with their own URL for every results page (for example ?cfp_my_query=2), so search engines can reach every page. Each page also gets its own canonical URL, including with Yoast SEO and Rank Math.
  • Improved : Caching & Debounce per Query : Query Cache, Cache Duration, and Debounce Delay moved from the global Settings page into each query (Query editor, Step 3 > Performance), so every query can use its own values. Existing queries keep using the previous global values until you change them. A cache duration of 0 is no longer allowed (it kept results forever); the minimum is now 60 seconds.
  • New : Clear Cache Button : A “Clear Cache” button in each query (Step 3 > Performance) removes that query’s cached results right away, so visitors get fresh data without waiting for the cache to expire. Other queries’ caches are left alone.
  • Fix : Cache Clearing with Object Cache : Saving a query or filter set now also clears cached results on sites that use a persistent object cache (such as Redis or Memcached), where they were previously kept until they expired.
  • Fix : Debounce Delay of 0 : A Debounce Delay of 0 no longer falls back to 300 ms.
  • Improved : Faster First Load : Pages with a grid no longer make any extra requests on load to fetch results or filter options.
  • Improved : Infinite Scroll Keyboard Access : Keyboard users now get a “Load more results” link with Infinite Scroll, shown when it is focused.
  • Fix : Special Characters on Cards : Titles, author names, and categories with apostrophes, quotes, dashes, or “&” (for example “Men’s Shirt”) no longer show as codes such as “’”.
  • Fix : Filter Sets Connected Query : Fixed the Filter Sets page not matching a filter set to its query, so the Connected Query column, the shortcode preview, and the taxonomy list now show the right query and only that post type’s taxonomies.
  • Fix : Admin Dashboard After Updates : Admin page scripts and styles now load with a version in their URL, so a cached file from an older version can no longer break the dashboard after an update.
  • Fix : Filter Sets Console Warning : Fixed a React “missing key” warning in the browser console on the Filter Sets list.
  • Fix : WordPress Version Requirement : Raised “Requires at least” to WordPress 6.2 to match the database queries the plugin uses.
  • Improved : Accessibility : Added screen reader labels to the frontend search box, dropdown and range filters, pagination buttons (including Previous/Next page), column switcher, and the admin toggle switches on the Settings, MCP, and Wishlist pages. Screen readers now announce the number of results after each filter change, and the “Clear all” button shows a visible keyboard focus ring.
  • Improved : Image Loading : Card images now download at the size they are actually shown instead of the full image width, which reduces page weight.
  • Improved : Translations : Frontend text such as “All {filter}”, “Search…”, “Page {number}”, result counts, column switcher labels, range filter placeholders, and error messages can now be translated.
  • Improved : RTL Support : The search icon, card badges, wishlist button, and filter counts now mirror correctly on right-to-left sites.
  • Improved : Code Standards : Cleaned up code to follow WordPress Coding Standards.

1.6.2

  • New: Layout/Style Option : Added a new Style tab to the settings page, allowing users to easily design and manage layouts and styles including colors, borders, shadows, and background colors.
  • New: Typography control : Added a new typography control for the style manager, letting you manage responsive options, size, weight, transform, style, line height, and letter spacing in one place.
  • New: Slider Dots Style Panel : Added new style controls for Slider Styles 1 and 2 to customize dot colors, active dot colors, size, active width, gap, and top spacing.
  • New: Slider Progress & Counter Style Panel : Added a new style panel for Slider Style 3 to customize bar color, fill color, height, counter color, and typography.
  • New: Card Background & Border Panel : Added a new Card Background panel in the Style sub-tab combining card background gradients, per-side borders, margin, padding, and shadows to replace the separate Border panel.
  • New : Clear Filters Button : Added a new “Clear Filters Button” option to the Filter Sets dropdown so users can drag and place it anywhere in the list with customizable text.
  • New : Clear Filters Shortcode : Added a new shortcode to place a standalone “Clear Filters” button anywhere on the page outside of the automatic filter bar.
  • New : Boutique Card Style Settings : Added a custom “Add to Bag Button Text” setting to Card Display Options for the Boutique card style, and moved Boutique to the top of the Card Style list.
  • New : Layout Preview Fallbacks : Added bundled illustration placeholders for card-style and masonry-tile previews in the Select Layout step on brand-new installs to replace bare photo icons.
  • New : Custom Color Picker : Replaced native browser color inputs in the Style sub-tab with a custom color picker featuring swatches, direct hex input, and a full hue/saturation/opacity picker with alpha channel support.
  • New : Slider Arrows Style Panel : Added a Slider Arrows panel to the Style tab (shown for the Slider layout) to customize arrow background color, icon color, border, shadow, padding, and margin across all three slider styles.
  • New : Active Filters Bar Setting : Added an option in Filter Sets to hide the “N filters active” bar shown above a filter set.
  • Improved : Gap in Card Background : Moved the card Gap (Spacing) control from the Layout tab into the Card Background panel of the Style tab, and the Add to Bag Button Text field now sits beside Columns instead of on its own row.
  • Improved : Card Image Size per Query : Card Image Size moved out of the global Settings page into each query (Query editor, Step 3, Layout tab, Card Image card), so every query can use its own image size. Existing queries keep using the previous global value until you change them.
  • Improved : Wishlist Pro Card : In the free version the whole “Account Wishlist (Database)” card on the Wishlist page is now a link that opens the Pro page in a new tab.
  • Improved : Insert Code Label : The “WordPress Shortcode” tab in the Insert Code step is now simply “Shortcode”.
  • Improved : Filter Sets Editor Display : Updated the Filter Sets editor to show friendly filter type names (such as “Pill Tabs”) instead of internal names.
  • Improved : Plugin Styles & Slider Behavior : Insulated plugin buttons, links, and pagination elements from theme styles to keep their layout intact, and updated the slider to move exactly one card or page per click.
  • Improved : Query Editor Navigation Buttons : Moved the Back, Next, and Finish buttons to the top of the step bar so they stay in view while scrolling, eliminating the need to scroll down.
  • Improved : Query Editor Step Bar : Added a soft glow effect to the current step in the Query editor’s step bar to make it easier to identify your current position.
  • Fix : Slider Arrows Alignment : Fixed Slider Style 1 arrows jumping on cards without featured images so they consistently align with the middle of the image area.
  • Fix : Default Query Names & Keys : Fixed an issue where new queries started blank by ensuring they now automatically default to sequential names and keys like “Query 1” and query_1.
  • Fix : Slider Spotlight Style : Fixed the empty gap beside the first and last card in Slider Style 2 and made next / previous slide smoothly instead of jumping.
  • Fix : Duplicate Query Key : Fixed the second grid staying on the loading spinner when the same Query Key is used more than once on a page (for example separate desktop and mobile grids).
  • Fix : Missing Queries : Fixed a query that existed in the database but did not appear on the Queries list and blocked its own Query Key as already in use.
  • Fix : Add to Bag Button : Fixed the Add to Bag button on product cards opening a raw JSON page instead of adding the product to the cart.
  • Fix : Loader Overlay : Fixed Spinner and Skeleton loaders appearing below the results instead of covering them while filtering.
  • Fix : Special Characters : Fixed category and term names containing “&” showing as “&” in filters and card labels.
  • Fix : Clear All and Range : Clear All now also resets Range filter values back to their full range.
  • Fix: Minor bug fixes and overall improvements for better stability and performance.

1.6.1

  • New: Account Wishlist integration – With Captain Advance Filter Pro’s Account Wishlist enabled, guest wishlist items are automatically synced to the user’s account upon login and cleared from the browser copy.
  • New: Slider layout – Style 1 (Equal Cards): displays equal-sized cards with side arrows and bottom dots for easy navigation.
  • New: Slider layout – Style 2 (Spotlight): enlarges the middle card while dimming the surrounding cards, with navigation arrows placed on the middle card.
  • New: Slider layout – Style 3 (Carousel): features a counter and top-right arrows accompanied by a bottom progress bar.
  • New: Pill Tabs filter – added support for using Pill Tabs as a display style for Radio and Checkbox filters.
  • New: Range filter slider – added a two-handle slider option to replace Min / Max number fields, complete with customizable step increments, live value readouts, and optional prefixes or suffixes.
  • New: Elegant Boutique card style (Pro) – a refined product card for jewelry and fashion stores with a large image, colour swatches, sale price, Quick Look chip, and a pill Add to Bag button. Listed in Card Style with a PRO tag in the free version, with an upgrade popup on click.
  • Improved: Insert Code step – redesigned the Query editor’s Insert Code step with one-click shortcode copying, ready-to-paste PHP snippets for child themes, and clear options to pick your embed method (Block Editor, Elementor, or PHP template).
  • Improved: Wishlist – added the [captaf-wishlist] shortcode directly to the Wishlist page row and repositioned the Wishlist menu item above Settings in the sidebar for easier access.
  • Fix: Show Count setting – Checkbox, Radio, and Pill Tabs filters now correctly respect the Show Count setting, ensuring counts only appear when enabled.
  • Fix: Filter reset on Clear All – “Clear All” now properly resets the visual selection state of Tab, Pill Tabs, Button, and Swatch filters so the “All” option lights up and previous choices are no longer highlighted.
  • Fix: Minor bug fixes and overall improvements for better stability and performance.

1.6.0

  • New: Wishlist – visitors can save items with a heart icon and browse them later on their own Wishlist page. Add it anywhere with the [captaf-wishlist] shortcode or the new “Captain Wishlist” Elementor widget. Saved items are kept in the visitor’s own browser (Local mode), so nothing is stored on your server. Turn it on or off from the new Wishlist page in the sidebar. An account-based (database) mode is available in Pro.
  • New: Boutique card style – a WooCommerce product card with a category label, sale / low-stock / bestseller / new badge, wishlist heart, price, title, short description, and a full-width Add to Bag button. Every part, including the wishlist heart and the Add to Bag button, can be switched on or off in Card Display Options.
  • Improved: If a query’s post type is no longer available (for example WooCommerce was deactivated), the Query editor now shows a warning, and site admins see a clear message on the front end instead of an empty grid.
  • New: Quick Support : Added a floating Panel providing direct access to free support tickets, changelog updates (“What’s New?”), Facebook community discussions, a feature request and bug reporting system, and a directory of other free Captain plugins.
  • Fix: Quick Support launcher was silently blocking clicks on the Query editor’s Back/Next buttons – its invisible click area was stretching to the full width of the (hidden) support dialog instead of just the button itself.
  • New: MCP Support : Added MCP support for AI assistants to read and manage queries, filter sets, and settings through the WordPress Abilities API.
  • Fix: Added missing translator comments for strings with placeholders, and preserved them through the production JS build so wp i18n make-pot no longer warns about undocumented placeholders.
  • Performance: All pages (Dashboard, Queries, Filter Sets, Settings, Docs, Help, Rollback, Our Products, White Label, Upgrade, MCP) are now code-split – only the app shell loads upfront, each page’s JS/CSS downloads on demand when the user opens it.
  • Fix: Minor bug fixes and overall improvements for better stability and performance.

short_description: Powerful AJAX filters for WordPress and WooCommerce with custom post type, taxonomy, meta, search, price, rating, and date filtering.
description:
Captain Advance Filter is a lightweight WordPress search and filter plugin that lets you create powerful AJAX powered filters for posts, pages, custom post types, and WooCommerce products.

Create advanced search and filtering experiences without coding. Build custom queries and filter sets, choose from multiple filter types and display styles, and show filtered results instantly without reloading the page.

Filter your content by categories, tags, custom taxonomies, post meta, product attributes, price, stock status, ratings, dates, and more. Display filter options using checkboxes, radio buttons, dropdowns, search fields, range sliders, A Z navigation, date pickers, WooCommerce ratings, or a frontend view switcher.

Use the visual Query Builder and Filter Set Builder to create reusable filtering systems, then display them anywhere using shortcodes, Gutenberg blocks, or Elementor widgets.

Watch the Plugin Overview Video | YouTube Tutorials | Facebook Community | X | Free Support

✨ Core Features:

  • AJAX Search & Filtering: Update results instantly without a page reload.
  • Visual Query Builder: Create custom queries for posts, pages, custom post types, and products.
  • Filter Set Builder: Combine multiple filters and connect them to a reusable query.
  • Multiple Filter Types: Checkbox, Radio, Pill Tabs, Dropdown, Search, Range, A Z, Date Picker, Woo Rating, and View Switcher.
  • Taxonomy & Meta Filtering: Filter content using categories, tags, custom taxonomies, custom fields, and post meta.
  • WooCommerce Product Filters: Filter products by attributes, price, stock status, and star ratings.
  • Multiple Display Styles: List, Buttons, Color Swatches, Image Swatches, Tabs, and Pill Tabs for supported filters.
  • AJAX Pagination: Choose from numbered Pagination, Load More, Infinite Scroll, or None.
  • SEO-Friendly Server-Side Rendering: The first page of results, pagination links, result counts, and filters are part of the page HTML, so search engines can read every result and visitors see content without waiting. Every results page has its own crawlable URL.
  • AJAX Loader Styles: Choose Spinner, Overlay, Skeleton, or None for AJAX result loading.
  • Frontend View Switcher: Let visitors switch between available grid column layouts.
  • Category & Search Archives: Place a grid in a category, tag, or WooCommerce product category template, or on the search results page, and it automatically shows only that archive’s posts.
  • Shareable Filter URLs: Share and bookmark filtered results with selected filter values preserved in the URL.
  • Result Count: Display the number of matching results with a dedicated shortcode.
  • Custom Result Cards: Choose from predefined card styles, including the new Boutique product card, or create custom card templates.
  • Wishlist: Let visitors save items with a heart icon and view them on a Wishlist page using a shortcode or Elementor widget.
  • Responsive Grid Layouts: Control desktop, tablet, and mobile columns.
  • Slider Layout: Show your cards as a slider with three styles: Equal Cards, Spotlight, and Carousel.
  • Style Controls: Design your cards from the Style tab with color pickers, responsive typography, borders, shadows, spacing, and slider arrow, dot, and progress styling.
  • Elementor Support: Dedicated Filter, Grid, Pagination, and Wishlist widgets.
  • Gutenberg Support: Native blocks for Filter, Grid, and Pagination.
  • Shortcode Support: Easily embed filters, grids, pagination, result counts, and the wishlist anywhere.
  • Query Caching: Optional caching using WordPress transients for faster repeated queries, set per query with its own cache duration and a one-click Clear Cache button.
  • Dark Mode: Clean and modern React powered admin dashboard with Dark Mode support.
  • No Coding Required: Build queries and filters directly from the WordPress admin dashboard.

🔎 Filter Types:

  • Checkbox: Select one or multiple options.
  • Radio: Select a single option.
  • Pill Tabs: A row of rounded tabs with an “All” tab first, ideal for a category switcher above your results.
  • Dropdown: Choose filter values from a dropdown.
  • Search: Search and filter content using keywords.
  • Range: Create numeric range filters such as price ranges, as Min / Max number fields or a two-handle slider.
  • A Z: Browse content alphabetically.
  • Date Picker: Filter content by publish date ranges.
  • Woo Rating: Filter WooCommerce products by star rating.
  • View Switcher: Allow visitors to switch between available result grid layouts.

🎨 Display Styles:

Checkbox and Radio filters can use multiple display styles depending on the selected data source:

  • List
  • Buttons
  • Color Swatches
  • Image Swatches
  • Tabs
  • Pill Tabs

Color and Image Swatches can automatically use WooCommerce attribute swatch data when available, with fallback options when swatch data is not configured.

📄 Pagination & Loading:

Choose how filtered results are displayed and loaded:

  • Pagination: Standard numbered pagination.
  • Load More: Load additional results without leaving the page.
  • Infinite Scroll: Automatically load more results while scrolling.
  • None: Display results without pagination controls.

Choose an AJAX loading indicator for each query:

  • Spinner
  • Overlay
  • Skeleton
  • None

🛒 WooCommerce Compatibility:

Captain Advance Filter works with WooCommerce and provides dedicated product filtering features.

  • Woo Rating: Filter products by N stars & up using WooCommerce product ratings.
  • Price Range: Filter products using WooCommerce price data.
  • Stock Status: Filter products by available stock status.
  • Product Attributes: Filter by attributes such as color, brand, size, and more.
  • Color Swatches: Display product attribute options as color swatches.
  • Image Swatches: Display product attribute options using images.
  • Shop Card: Display WooCommerce product price, sale badge, and Add to Cart button.
  • Boutique Card: A product card with a category label, badges, wishlist heart, price, description, and an Add to Bag button whose label you can change. Captain Advance Filter Pro adds a second, more refined style called Elegant Boutique.
  • Custom Product Templates: Use WooCommerce specific tokens such as {{price}}, {{sale_badge}}, and {{add_to_cart}}.

🧩 Custom Post Type Support:

Use Captain Advance Filter with any publicly viewable WordPress post type. Create custom queries and filter results using taxonomies, post meta, dates, search terms, and other supported filter sources.

🔌 Builder Integrations:

  • Elementor: Dedicated Filter, Grid, Pagination, and Wishlist widgets with Elementor styling controls.
  • Gutenberg: Native blocks for Filter, Grid, and Pagination.
  • Shortcodes: Use Captain Advance Filter with any WordPress page builder or theme that supports shortcodes.
  • Bricks Builder: Support coming soon.

⚡ Performance:

  • Lightweight frontend implementation.
  • AJAX powered filtering without full page reloads.
  • Frontend assets are loaded only on pages where Captain Advance Filter is used.
  • No jQuery dependency on the frontend.
  • Optional query result caching using WordPress transients.
  • Native lazy loading support for result card images.

🔗 Shortcodes:

  • [captaf-filter id="1"] : Display a filter set.
  • [captaf-grid query="query_key"] : Display the filtered content grid.
  • [captaf-pagination query="query_key"] : Display pagination controls.
  • [captaf-count query="query_key"] : Display the matching result count.
  • [captaf-wishlist] : Display the visitor’s saved wishlist items.
  • [captaf-clear-filters query="query_key"] : A standalone “Clear Filters” button you can place anywhere on the page – top, bottom, wherever – instead of relying on the automatic active-filters bar above the filter widget. Optional text="Reset" for custom button text, hide_empty="no" to keep it always visible instead of only appearing once a filter is active.

You can also display individual filters from a Filter Set using the only attribute.
